stories.headline: SP decides not a field a third candidate for the Rajya Sabha election
stories.title: SP decides not a field a third candidate for the Rajya Sabha election
stories.summary: The focus is on the Assembly election, Akhilesh Yadav says, with the party preparing to contest all the Assembly seats
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) decided not to field a third candidate for the forthcoming Rajya Sabha election, paving the way for all 10 seats from Uttar Pradesh to be filled without a contest.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the SP engaged in political slugfest over the development, with the ruling BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ridiculing the Opposition party, while the SP hit back to say the real target was the Assembly election in early 2027.

“Now our focus is not on three (Rajya Sabha nominations), but on 403 (the number of seats in the U.P. Assembly),” Mr. Yadav said on social media platform X, with the party deciding to focus its energy on the forthcoming Assembly election, having analysed the current political situation.
The SP national president’s post made it clear that the party was preparing to contest all Assembly seats.

“Our national president made it clear again and again that the number of seats was not the issue but the winnability of candidates with the objective of forming the government in 2027 by defeating the BJP,” senior SP leader Sudhir Panwar said.

The SP was not going to boycott the Assembly election due to the controversies surrounding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Mr. Panwar said, adding, “People will throw out both the BJP and the Chief Election Commissioner in the near future.”
The SP has nominated senior leader Ram Gopal Yadav and industrialist Dhanraj Nathwani as its candidates in the Rajya Sabha election.
Earlier last week, Mr. Yadav had indicated the party would contest three seats.
The SP has eight fewer MLAs than it needs to have a third member elected.
U.P. Minister of Panchayati Raj Om Prakash Rajbhar targeted the SP on social media platform X. “My friend Akhilesh, it’s all done, just snap.
Well, sometimes, even if it’s just a matter of time, you still do something sensible.
Like you did today.

stories.headline: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar on Tuesday warned that the Congress would not remain silent if eligible voters were denied their fundamental right to vote, even as Telangana Youth Congress cadres staged a protest outside the State Chief Electoral Officer’s office here demanding the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Speaking to the media at Sriramulapalli in Koheda mandal of Siddipet district, Mr. Prabhakar alleged that votes of poor and eligible people in rural areas were being removed in the name of revision of electoral rolls.
He accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) failing to function independently and alleged that it was acting under the influence of the Centre.

He condemned the detention of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi during their protest in Delhi against alleged irregularities in the electoral process, describing the action as undemocratic.
He said the Congress would intensify its ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from the village level to protect the voting rights of every citizen.
Meanwhile, Telangana Youth Congress president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy led the protest outside the Telangana CEO’s office and demanded his immediate arrest.
Mr. Reddy alleged that the CEC was acting in the interests of the BJP and RSS and claimed that nearly 14 crore votes had been removed across the country without due procedure.
He said the Youth Congress would organise protests across Telangana seeking the resignation of Mr. Kumar.
He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the Centre failed to respond to their demands.
Separately, leaders of INDIA bloc parties staged a protest outside the Hyderabad Collectorate demanding the removal and arrest of Mr. Kumar.
They submitted a representation to the Joint Collector and said their agitation would continue until the CEC was removed and a thorough investigation ordered.

Meanwhile, Congress Khairatabad district president M. Rohit, Secunderabad district president Deepak Jain, MLC Kodandaram, CPI State leader Narasimha, CPI(M) city secretary Venkatesh, Telangana Jana Samithi (TJS) leaders Salim Pasha and Arun Kumar, Hyderabad district president Narsaiah and representatives of the VCK participated in the protest.

stories.title: RBI approves merger of Emirates NBD’s India branches with RBL Bank from 1 December
stories.summary: The move consolidates the Dubai-based lender’s Indian operations with RBL Bank after its over ₹26,000-crore acquisition of a 60% stake, as the private lender plans to expand branches and deepen its corporate and wealth businesses.

article_sentences: MUMBAI: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved the merger of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C.’s Indian branches with RBL Bank, effective 1 December, consolidating the two banks’ Indian operations after the Dubai-based lender acquired a majority stake in the private sector bank earlier this year.
The approval brings Emirates NBD’s three Indian branches under RBL Bank, following the completion of an over ₹26,000 crore transaction that made the foreign lender the promoter of RBL Bank.

“RBI sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. (Transferor Bank) with RBL Bank Limited (Transferee Bank),” the central bank said in a release, adding that all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as branches of RBL Bank from 1 December 2026.
The merger takes effect on 1 December 2026.
From that date, all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as RBL Bank branches.
Emirates NBD’s three Indian branches—in Mumbai, Gurugram and Chennai—will become part of RBL Bank.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Demolition Of CSI Church Built As Community Hall In Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi District
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Demolition Of CSI Church Built As Community Hall In Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi District
stories.summary: The Collector had refused to recognise the community hall as a place of worship citing communal tensions between Hindu and Christian residents.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Collector had refused to recognise the community hall as a place of worship citing communal tensions between Hindu and Christian residents.

The Supreme Court on Friday (October 16) stayed the demolition of a Church of South India (CSI) church in Thippanampatti village in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district, in a plea challenging the High Court order finding the structure unauthorised and ordering its restoration as a community hall.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Singh issued notice on the plea filed by the church trust.
Senior Advocate Huzefa Ahmadi appeared for the church trust.

The case concerns a building constructed by the Tirunelveli Diocesan Trust Association, which was granted permission in 2014 to construct a community hall called the “Church of South India Community Hall”.
The association contends that the building has since been used as a church by the local Christian community, with regular prayers and religious services being conducted peacefully.
The Trust on March 4, 2024, sought recognition of the community hall as a place of worship and permission for the church tower.
However, the District Collector rejected the application on June 25, 2024, refusing permission to convert the community hall into a church and to construct the tower.
The Collector's decision was challenged by the Trust before the Madras High Court.
Before the High Court, the State argued that the original permission covered only a community hall and no approval had been obtained for a spire erected on the building.

Relying on Rule 4(3) of the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Building Rules, 1997, the State submitted that prior approval of the District Collector was mandatory for a site intended to be used for public worship or religious purposes.
The rule permits the Collector to refuse approval if the proposed use is likely to endanger public peace and order.

stories.headline: Delhi Protest | Supreme Court Refuses To Examine Challenge To Section 163 BNSS, Issues Notice On Plea Challenging S. 172 BNSS
stories.title: Delhi Protest | Supreme Court Refuses To Examine Challenge To Section 163 BNSS, Issues Notice On Plea Challenging S. 172 BNSS
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: In the pleas arising from the recent Delhi protests, the Supreme Court on Thursday (October 15) said that it will not examine constitutional validity of Section 163 of BNSS, 2023 (erstwhile Section 144 of CrPC), which empowers executive magistrates to issue prohibitory orders.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of Section 144 CrPC, the provision corresponding to Section 163 BNSS, in Babulal Parate.
State of Maharashtra, (1961) 3 SCR 423.

The Court, however, notice on a challenge to Section 172 BNSS(which was not there in CrPC), which empowers police officers to detain or remove people who resist, refuse or disregard their directions, and directed the Union Government to file its reply within two weeks.
“Oral submissions were made with regard to the vires of Section 163 BNSS.
However, as the pari materia provision of Section 144 CrPC has been upheld in Babulal Parate.
State of Maharashtra, (1961) 3 SCR 423, we are not inclined to entertain the same.
Accordingly, issue notice, returnable on 19.11.2026, only on the limited issue pertaining to the constitutionality of Section 172 BNSS,” the Court observed.
Section 172(1) BNSS requires people to comply with lawful directions issued by a police officer in the discharge of duties under Chapter XII, which deals with preventive action by the police.

Section 172(2) empowers a police officer to detain or remove anyone who resists, refuses, ignores or disregards such a direction, and either take the person before a Magistrate or release them as soon as possible within 24 hours in petty cases.

The petition argues that the provision allows detention on the basis of a police officer's subjective assessment, without requiring reasonable apprehension of a cognizable offence, recorded reasons or adequate safeguards for judicial scrutiny.
The writ petition seeks a declaration that Section 172 violates Articles 14, 19 and 21, which guarantee equality before law, fundamental freedoms and protection of life and personal liberty.

stories.headline: India’s blind women cricketers still wait for house sites and jobs a year after their World Cup win
stories.title: India’s blind women cricketers still wait for house sites and jobs a year after their World Cup win
stories.summary: Captain Deepika T.C. of Madakasira in Andhra Pradesh’s Sri Sathya Sai district is still waiting for the house site she was promised
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Deepika T.C. captained India to victory in the first Women’s T20 World Cup for the Blind in November 2025.
Nearly a year later, she is still waiting for the house site that leaders and officials promised her.
She and her 15 teammates, who won the tournament hosted jointly by India and Sri Lanka, say they are unable to get the support they need from society and the government in their day-to-day lives.
They do not get playgrounds and fitness guidance in their localities, and they cannot afford training in big cities.
Leaders who make tall promises in public have shown little interest in ensuring government jobs and house sites for them, they said.
Ms. Deepika hails from Madakasira in Sri Sathya Sai district.
“Due to our partial vision issues, we cannot move around government offices to follow up on house site issues.
The government has to do its own and instill confidence among us,” she told.
The Hindu.
Ms. Deepika, who developed vision problems as an infant, completed a degree course and focused on cricket in spite of her family’s financial struggles.
Her parents, Timmappa and Chittemma, encouraged her to practise cricket in Bengaluru although they had many fears about her partial vision.
She has been consistently playing well and won special recognition when she scored 92 runs off 45 balls against Australia in a World Cup match.

stories.headline: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.title: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.summary: The consideration involved is an equity investment of over Rs ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India Cements on Thursday said that the company has entered into energy supply and share subscription agreement to acquire 3.62 per cent equity shares of Zenataris Renewable Energy Private Ltd, a company engaged in generation and transmission of renewable energy.

“The acquisition is for the purposes of meeting India Cements’ green energy needs, optimising energy cost and comply with regulatory requirements for captive power consumption under electricity laws,” the company said in a filing to the exchanges.
The consideration involved is an equity investment of over ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement.

Zenataris is based in Hyderabad, and is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) established for the development and operation of Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) hybrid renewable energy project located at Kudligi, Vijayanagara District, Karnataka.
The SPV shall supply 11 MW renewable energy to the cement plants of India Cements on a group captive basis, a statement filed by India Cements to the exchanges said.

stories.headline: India's $100 billion China trade deficit: Are non-tariff barriers blocking Indian exports?
stories.title: India's $100 billion China trade deficit: Are non-tariff barriers blocking Indian exports?
stories.summary: Speaking at an interaction in Bangkok, Sitharaman said China's restrictions were preventing Indian products from realising their potential in one of the world's largest markets.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: “With China, I think our trade balance is against us, and it is growing exponentially,” Sitharaman said.
She added that China “uses non-tariff barriers unhesitatingly” and that this was “the biggest hurdle in the in the trade between India and China.”
Sitharaman pointed to phytosanitary regulations, which are intended to prevent the spread of plant pests and diseases, as one of the barriers affecting Indian exporters.
She said Indian products, including generic medicines, beef and vegetables, had “immense” potential in the Chinese market but faced restrictions.
Non-tariff barriers can include licensing requirements, product standards, testing procedures and sanitary or phytosanitary measures.

While such regulations can serve legitimate health and safety objectives, differences in implementation and market-access requirements can increase compliance costs and make it harder for exporters to enter foreign markets.
For Indian businesses, improving access to China could create opportunities across pharmaceuticals and agricultural products.

However, the extent to which these barriers account for the trade deficit would need to be assessed alongside other factors, including the competitiveness of Indian products and the composition of bilateral trade.
Sitharaman said India had refrained from imposing retaliatory non-tariff restrictions or countervailing duties on Chinese goods, despite the widening imbalance.

The finance minister's remarks come as New Delhi and Beijing seek to stabilise relations following the border confrontation in 2020, which triggered prolonged diplomatic tensions and restrictions on Chinese investments and business activities.
Both countries have since taken steps to ease tensions and resume high-level engagement.
However, trade remains a contentious area, with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also recently saying India was not “getting a level playing field in China.”
